formation.title: The Kingdom of Kongo Reborn
formation.text:
The great work is complete. From the banks of the mighty Nzadi, the river the foreigners call Congo, to the shores of the western ocean, the scattered provinces once more answer to a single throne. Mbanza Kongo stands as the heart of a reunited realm, its stone churches and ancient spirit houses alike testament to a kingdom that bridges worlds.

The Manikongo must now choose the path forward. Shall we embrace the connections forged with the kingdoms across the sea, using their faith and learning to strengthen our own? Or shall we look inward, to the iron traditions and ancestral wisdom that built this kingdom long before any foreign ship appeared on our horizon?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We shall walk with Rome and Lisbon.

modifiers.name: Christian Diplomacy of Kongo
modifiers.text: The Manikongo has embraced the faith of Rome, opening channels of diplomacy with the courts of Europe. Kongolese envoys travel to Lisbon and the Vatican, while missionaries and scholars bring knowledge and techniques to Mbanza Kongo.

options.text: Our strength is in the forge and the ancestors.

modifiers.name: Strength of the Ancestors
modifiers.text: The Manikongo draws authority from the traditions of the founders: the master blacksmiths who forged the kingdom. The drums of war echo across the provinces, and the shield warriors stand ready to defend every border.

advances.name: Iron Mastery
advances.text: The founders of Kongo were masters of the forge, and the blacksmith remains a figure of spiritual and political authority. Iron tools, weapons, and symbols of kingship flow from Kongolese smithies.

advances.name: Shield Warriors
advances.text: The heavy infantry of Kongo carry large shields and swords into battle, forming a disciplined core that absorbs enemy charges before counterattacking at close quarters.

advances.name: Nzo a Nkisi Tradition
advances.text: The spirit houses of Kongo are repositories of nkisi: sacred objects charged with spiritual power. These shrines anchor communities and reinforce the authority of local leaders.

advances.name: Raffia Weaving
advances.text: Kongolese weavers transform raffia palm fibers into luxurious cloth with tight weaves and intricate patterns, dyed and embroidered to a standard that makes the cloth a reliable medium of exchange.

advances.name: Nzimbu Shell Currency
advances.text: The spiral nzimbu shells from Luanda serve as the kingdom's standardized currency. One hundred buy a hen, two thousand a goat: a sophisticated monetary system that facilitates trade across the realm.

advances.name: Pombo Scouts
advances.text: Elite scouting troops of the Kongo army, the pombos are trained to keep pace with mounted riders on foot. They serve as the kingdom's eyes and ears, pursuing fleeing enemies and reconnoitering enemy positions.

advances.name: Stone Masonry
advances.text: Under Afonso I, Kongolese workers learned European stone construction techniques, raising churches and palaces that blended imported methods with local sensibilities: a physical testament to the kingdom's cultural synthesis.

advances.name: Royal School of Mbanza Kongo
advances.text: By 1516, over a thousand students attended the royal school at Mbanza Kongo, with additional schools established in the provinces. The result was a fully literate noble class unprecedented in sub-Saharan Africa. Its teachers, the mestres, are Kongolese nobles themselves.

advances.name: Mbanza Kongo
advances.text: The capital of the kingdom grows into a true city, its streets named, its stone cathedrals and chapels rising alongside traditional structures. Mbanza Kongo is the political, spiritual, and economic heart of the realm.

advances.name: Provincial Dukes
advances.text: The six great provinces (Nsundi, Mpangu, Mbata, Soyo, Mbamba, and Mpemba) are organized under appointed governors who bear European-style ducal titles, creating a structured hierarchy of administration.

advances.name: Copper Trade
advances.text:
The copper deposits of the region fuel a trade in worked metal that stretches across Central Africa and beyond, providing the kingdom with a valuable commodity alongside its textile and ivory exports.

Available in: Iron Forge

advances.name: Musket Regiment
advances.text: Kongolese troops trained in the use of European firearms form organized musket regiments, combining imported military technology with indigenous tactical traditions.

advances.name: Atlantic Diplomacy
advances.text: The kingdom's envoys navigate the complex politics of the Atlantic world, engaging with Portuguese, Dutch, and papal courts. Kongolese ambassadors are received in Lisbon and Rome, establishing the kingdom as a recognized sovereign power.

advances.name: Cloth Market Tradition
advances.text: Dedicated markets for the trade of raffia cloth emerge in the kingdom's towns, where the libongo, standardized cloth currency, changes hands alongside imported European goods and regional commodities.

advances.name: Missionary Education
advances.text: Jesuit and Capuchin missionaries establish colleges in the kingdom, teaching reading, writing, theology, and European sciences. The resulting literate class bridges the gap between Kongolese and European knowledge traditions.

advances.name: Battle Drums and Signals
advances.text: A complex system of drums, horns, and pennants allows Kongolese commanders to coordinate their forces across the battlefield, directing the center and two wings of their battle formations with precision.

advances.name: Three-Division Tactics
advances.text: Kongolese armies deploy in a sophisticated three-division formation, a strong center flanked by two mobile wings, coordinated through an elaborate system of drum signals and battle flags.

advances.name: Mbanza Fortifications
advances.text: Key towns and strategic positions receive defensive fortifications, combining indigenous stockade construction with techniques learned from European military engineering.

advances.name: Syncretic Faith
advances.text: The Kongolese practice of Christianity incorporates elements of traditional belief, creating a distinctive religious culture that acknowledges both the cross and the nkisi. This synthesis strengthens social cohesion across diverse communities.

advances.name: Lucanzos
advances.text: Special detachments called lucanzos are trained for raiding, ambush, and unconventional warfare. These elite troops operate independently, striking where the enemy is weakest and withdrawing before a decisive engagement.

advances.name: Long-Distance Trade
advances.text: Kongolese merchants extend their networks deep into the interior, trading cloth, copper, salt, and ivory along routes that connect the Atlantic coast to the heart of Central Africa.

advances.name: The Antonine Movement
advances.text: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita's Antonine movement proclaims a distinctly Kongolese Christianity, teaching that the sacred figures of the faith were Kongolese. Though its prophetess is martyred, the movement's message of cultural pride endures.

event.title: The Prophetess of Kongo
event.text:
A young woman of noble birth has risen from the ashes of decades of civil war, claiming to be possessed by the spirit of Saint Anthony. But her teachings are no simple repetition of European doctrine: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita proclaims that Jesus Christ was born in Mbanza Kongo, that the Mother of God was a Kongolese woman, and that the saints were the ancestors of the Kongolese people.

Her Antonine movement sweeps through the countryside, offering hope to a people exhausted by war. She calls for the reunification of the kingdom and the restoration of the abandoned capital. Thousands flock to her banner, and the old powers, both Kongolese and European, watch with unease.

options.text: Let her message unite our people.

modifiers.name: Antonine Fervor
modifiers.text: The teachings of the prophetess have spread through the land, proclaiming that the kingdom's sacred roots run deeper than any foreign creed. The people rally around this vision of a distinctly Kongolese faith.

options.text: Channel her followers' zeal into service of the kingdom.

modifiers.name: Antonine Mobilization
modifiers.text: The fervor of the Antonine movement channels into service of the kingdom, as Kimpa Vita's followers rally to the Manikongo's banner with the devotion of the faithful.

advances.name: Civil War Resilience
advances.text: The kingdom endures fifty years of devastating civil war following the Battle of Mbwila. Though battered, the idea of Kongo as a unified realm never dies, and the people's resilience sees them through the darkest years.

advances.name: Restored Kingdom
advances.text: After decades of fragmentation, the kingdom is gradually reunified under renewed royal authority. The provinces once again acknowledge a central Manikongo, and the machinery of governance is rebuilt.

advances.name: Coastal Defense
advances.text: As European powers grow more aggressive along the coast, Kongo fortifies its borders and strategic positions, making any invasion a costly proposition for would-be conquerors.

advances.name: Ivory Export
advances.text: Ivory becomes one of the kingdom's most lucrative exports, processed and traded to European merchants who prize the material for luxury goods. The trade enriches the kingdom's coffers and sustains its economy.

advances.name: Kongolese Identity
advances.text: In an age of revolutionary change, the people of Kongo reassert their unique cultural heritage: the textile arts, iron traditions, drum languages, and governance systems that define their civilization.

event.title: The Kongolese Identity
event.text:
As the age of revolutions reshapes the world, the people of Kongo look to their own heritage with renewed pride. The raffia cloth patterns that once served as currency, the iron-forging traditions that gave birth to kings, the drum signals that coordinated armies across vast distances: these are not relics of a vanished past but living traditions that define who the Kongolese are.

Scholars and elders work to preserve and celebrate the kingdom's unique cultural legacy, ensuring that the identity of Kongo endures regardless of what changes the future may bring.

modifiers.name: Kongolese Renaissance
modifiers.text: A renewed sense of Kongolese identity surges through the kingdom, as the people rediscover and celebrate the traditions, arts, and governance systems that make their civilization unique.

options.text: Our people's pride shall become our strength in arms.

modifiers.name: National Mobilization
modifiers.text: The renewed pride of the Kongolese people translates into military readiness, as warriors who fight for their cultural heritage fight with a determination born of deep identity.

advances.name: Modern Army
advances.text: The Kongolese military embraces modern training methods, tactics, and organization, creating a professional force capable of defending the kingdom's sovereignty in a changing world.

advances.name: Spirit of Independence
advances.text: As colonial pressures mount across Africa, the Kongolese draw on centuries of proud sovereignty to resist foreign domination, maintaining the kingdom's independence and territorial integrity.

advances.name: Palm Oil Economy
advances.text: The transition to palm oil as a major export commodity diversifies the kingdom's economy, providing a sustainable revenue source as traditional trade patterns shift in the industrial age.

destiny.name: The Reunited Kingdom
destiny.text: The scattered provinces answer to a single Manikongo once more. Now the kingdom must choose its path: outward to the wider world, or inward to the forge and the ancestors.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Kingdom Restored
event.text: The drums sound from Mbanza Kongo to the farthest provinces. The Manikongo sits upon a throne that was never truly lost, only contested. Now the kingdom stands united once more, ready to write the next chapter of its long history.

options.text: Let the drums carry our triumph.

destiny.name: The Embassy to Rome
destiny.text: Establish Kongo as a recognized Christian kingdom by building diplomatic and institutional ties with Europe. Found a chancery in the capital to write the kingdom's letters to Lisbon and Rome, as Afonso I did, and develop the ivory trade to finance this ambition.

conditions.text: Chose Christian Diplomacy of Kongo
A Chancery stands in our capital (the capital must be a town)
A market the country is in

children.text: Ivory is produced in the market
Ivory is traded in the market

conditions.text: Gold at least 1000

event.title: Envoys Across the Sea
event.text: Kongolese ambassadors have been received in the courts of Europe, presenting gifts of ivory and fine raffia cloth. Our chancery writes to the kings of Europe as an equal, and the scholars of Mbanza Kongo study the learning and laws of the West, adapting what serves the kingdom and discarding what does not. The Manikongo is recognized as a sovereign among sovereigns.

options.text: Our voice is heard in the halls of power.

destiny.name: The Atlantic Trade Network
destiny.text: Extend Kongolese control over the Atlantic coast by securing the island of Sao Tome and the port of Gabun, and by raising Mbanza Soyo, the kingdom's own harbour on the great river, into a town. A trade network will connect the interior to the world.

conditions.text: Own São Tomé, or a subject owns it
Own Gabun, or a subject owns it
Mbanza Soyo is ours and has grown into a town
Gold at least 2000

event.title: Masters of the Atlantic Coast
event.text: Kongolese ships and merchants now dominate the trade routes from Sao Tome to the Gabun coast. Ivory, copper, and fine cloth flow outward while European goods, knowledge, and currency flow in. The question now is how to use this wealth: to build a merchant fleet that rivals any in the Atlantic, or to invest in the schools and institutions that will secure the kingdom's future for generations.

options.text: Build the fleet and fill it with ivory.

modifiers.name: Ivory Fleet
modifiers.text: Kongolese merchant vessels laden with ivory, copper, and raffia cloth ply the Atlantic trade routes, enriching the kingdom's coffers and extending its commercial reach.

modifiers.name: Mission Schools
modifiers.text: Schools established through partnerships with European missionaries spread literacy and institutional knowledge through the provinces of Kongo.

destiny.name: Kongo and Christendom
destiny.text: Achieve the ultimate expression of Kongo's diplomatic vision: take Lisbon itself, build a dock at Soyo to sail the new ocean routes, and prove that the Manikongo stands as an equal among the monarchs of Christendom.

conditions.text: Own Lisbon, or a subject owns it
Mbanza Soyo is ours and a Dock, Dry Dock, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard or Naval Base stands there
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Manikongo in Lisbon
event.text: What was once unthinkable is now reality: the banner of Kongo flies over Lisbon itself, and the Manikongo's ambassador walks the halls of the Vatican as an equal. The kingdom that the Portuguese once thought to patronize has surpassed its would-be tutors. The question now is whether to formalize this new standing through papal recognition and diplomatic prestige, or to use it as a foundation for a commercial empire that spans the Atlantic.

modifiers.name: Papal Recognition
modifiers.text: The Pope has formally recognized the Manikongo as a sovereign Christian monarch, granting Kongo a diplomatic standing that commands respect across Christendom.

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes of Kongo
modifiers.text: The merchant elite of Kongo have risen to positions of enormous influence, their trading networks spanning the Atlantic and generating wealth that reshapes the kingdom's economy.

destiny.name: Master of the Interior
destiny.text: Kongolese authority is pushed beyond the traditional six provinces into the Congo basin interior. The Teke are subdued, the Pool region is held at Boma, and iron forges are lit in three of the kingdom's towns to arm the advance.

event.title: Beyond the Six Provinces
event.text: The armies of the Manikongo have crossed the boundaries of the traditional six provinces and planted the kingdom's banner in the lands of the Teke and the peoples of the great river's Pool region. The interior is opening before us, and the riches of the Congo basin lie within reach.

destiny.name: The Lunda March
destiny.text: The copper-rich heartland of the Lunda is entered. Mussumba, the Katanga region and Kazembe on the far side of the copper country are taken, and the wealth of the interior fuels the empire's ambitions.

conditions.text: Own Mussumba, or a subject owns it
Own Katanga, or a subject owns it
Own Kazembe, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Wealth of the Lunda
event.text: The great march into the interior has reached the copper lands of the Lunda. Mussumba, seat of the Mwata Yamvo, has fallen to Kongolese arms, and the mines of Katanga now feed the royal treasury. This wealth can be extracted as tribute to fuel further expansion, or the veterans who conquered it can be honored and retained as an elite corps hardened by years of jungle campaigning.

modifiers.name: Copper Tribute
modifiers.text: The conquered Lunda territories pay tribute in copper and other metals, enriching the royal treasury at the cost of diplomatic goodwill with neighbors.

modifiers.name: Jungle Veterans
modifiers.text: Veterans of the grueling campaigns through the Congo basin's forests have become an elite fighting force, hardened by years of jungle warfare and utterly loyal to the Manikongo.

destiny.name: Heart of Africa
destiny.text: The entire Congo basin is commanded, from the cataracts of Nyangwe to the northern reaches at Bangui. Mbanza Kongo stands as a city at its centre and iron forges burn in ten towns: the greatest empire Central Africa has ever seen.

event.title: Empire of the Congo
event.text: From the cataracts of Nyangwe to the northern reaches of Bangui, from the Atlantic coast to the copper mines of the far interior: the Manikongo commands an empire that spans the heart of Africa. No kingdom south of the Sahara has ever united so vast a territory under one throne. The iron crown of the founder-smiths now sits upon the brow of a true emperor. How shall this empire be governed: through the absolute authority of the iron throne, or through the network of rivers that binds this vast realm together?

modifiers.name: The Iron Throne
modifiers.text: The Manikongo rules as absolute emperor from the iron throne, the ancient symbol of the master smiths who founded the kingdom transformed into the seat of continental power. The electors of the great lineages are no longer asked, and they resent it.

options.text: Command the rivers, command the realm.

modifiers.name: River Kings
modifiers.text: The empire is governed through the network of rivers that connects its vast territories, with regional governors commanding the waterways that serve as highways binding the realm together.

units.name: Shield Warriors
units.text: Heavy Kongolese infantry armed with large shields and swords. These disciplined troops form the defensive backbone of the army, absorbing enemy volleys before closing for decisive hand-to-hand combat.

units.name: Pombo Scouts
units.text: Elite pursuit troops trained to keep pace with mounted riders on foot. The pombos serve as scouts, skirmishers, and pursuers, using their exceptional speed and knowledge of terrain to outmaneuver the enemy.

units.name: Kongolese Musket Regiment
units.text: Organized musket troops combining European firearms with Kongolese tactical discipline. By the seventeenth century, Kongo fielded hundreds of trained musketeers alongside traditional forces.

units.name: Lucanzos
units.text: Special detachment troops trained for raiding, ambush, and unconventional warfare. The lucanzos strike fast and disappear, disrupting enemy supply lines and sowing confusion in hostile territory.

units.name: Modern Kongolese Infantry
units.text: Professionally trained Kongolese infantry equipped with modern weapons and tactics, representing the kingdom's adaptation to the military realities of the industrial age.

buildings.name: Iron Forge
buildings.text: A traditional Kongolese smithy where master blacksmiths produce weapons, tools, and the iron symbols of royal authority. The forge is both workshop and sacred space.

buildings.name: Nzo a Nkisi
buildings.text: A traditional Kongolese spirit house containing nkisi: sacred objects believed to channel spiritual power. These shrines serve as centers of community life and reinforcements of local authority.

buildings.name: Stone Church
buildings.text: A church constructed in the style pioneered by Afonso I, blending European stone masonry with Kongolese architectural sensibilities. These buildings are both houses of worship and symbols of the kingdom's engagement with the wider world.

buildings.name: Cloth Market
buildings.text: A dedicated market for the trade of raffia cloth, where the libongo currency changes hands and merchants from across the kingdom gather to exchange goods.

buildings.name: Mpusu Looms
buildings.text: Upright looms on which the leaf fibre of the raffia palm is woven into mpusu, the patterned cloth of Kongo. Portuguese visitors set the best of it beside velvet and damask. Bundles of it pass as money across the kingdom.

where.text: Fiber Crops is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Ivory Carvers
buildings.text: Workshops where tusks from the interior are cut into horns, bracelets and lidded boxes, carved with the same interlace as the raffia cloths. Horns of this work were given to the courts of Europe and kept by the Medici.

where.text: Ivory is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: School of the Mestres
buildings.text: A school in the manner of the royal school at Mbanza Kongo, where lay teachers of noble birth, the mestres, teach the sons of the nobility to read and write Portuguese and Latin and to keep the faith in their home provinces.

buildings.name: Jesuit College
buildings.text: An educational institution established by Jesuit missionaries, teaching literacy, theology, and European sciences to the sons of the Kongolese nobility.

buildings.name: Mbanza Fortress
buildings.text: A defensive fortification combining indigenous stockade construction with European military engineering, protecting the kingdom's key towns and strategic positions.

buildings.name: Antonine Shrine
buildings.text: A place of worship dedicated to the Antonine tradition, where the teachings of Kimpa Vita, that the sacred figures of Christianity were Kongolese, are preserved and celebrated.

buildings.name: Palm Oil Press
buildings.text: Mortars, boiling pots and fires beside the oil palm groves, where village households pound the fruit and render its oil for the caravans to the coast. The palm harvest of the land grows with the trade.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fruit

buildings.name: Embassy House
buildings.text: A grand diplomatic residence where Kongolese and foreign envoys meet, combining European architectural elements with Kongolese design. It serves as both embassy and cultural showcase.

buildings.name: Royal Forge
buildings.text: The supreme forge of the Manikongo, where the finest iron and copper are worked into weapons, regalia, and tools of empire. Master smiths perform sacred rituals as they shape the metals that symbolize royal authority.

list.name: Mwene Provinces
list.text: The Manikongo divides the realm into six provinces (Soyo, Mpemba, Mbamba, Mpangu, Mbata, and Nsundi) each governed by a mani appointed and rotated at the throne's pleasure. The mani-governors hold delegated military, fiscal, and judicial powers but remain salaried agents of the king. The system gave Afonso I unprecedented administrative reach into the Congo basin; left unmaintained, governors entrenched into rival courts, as Soyo did from the late seventeenth century onward.

list.name: Kanda Council
list.text: The mwisikongo aristocracy was organized into matrilineal kanda lineages whose senior heads (the Mwene Vunda, Mwene Mbata, and Mwene Soyo prominent among them) held the right to elect each new Manikongo. Kongolese succession was elective, not strictly hereditary, and the council bound the throne to its great clans. When the council fractured at the Battle of Mbwila in 1665, the kingdom collapsed into a forty-year civil war among Kimpanzu and Kinlaza claimants.

list.name: Nzimbu Royal Monopoly
list.text: The nzimbu, small marine snail shells harvested under royal monopoly from the island of Luanda Bay, served as the kingdom's currency, sized and counted into pots of fixed denomination. The Manikongo extracted an annual head tax in nzimbu from every adult male and redistributed the shells as titles, salaries, and tribute. The Portuguese seizure of Luanda in 1576 and the flooding of the market with Brazilian cowries destroyed the monopoly within a generation.

conditions.text: Own Luanda, or a subject owns it

list.name: Royal Chancery of Mbanza Kongo
list.text: Afonso I Mvemba a Nzinga (r.1509-1542) founded a permanent literate chancery at Mbanza Kongo that produced over four hundred surviving Portuguese and Latin letters to the kings of Portugal, the popes in Rome, and Kongo's own provincial governors. Staffed by mission-trained Kongolese scribes alongside a small corps of Portuguese clerics, the chancery archived treaties, drafted royal decrees, and sustained the embassies to Lisbon. By Garcia II's reign (1641-1661) it negotiated directly with the Dutch and the Spanish Habsburgs.

conditions.text: Catholicism religion

list.name: São Salvador Confraternities
list.text: After the elevation of Mbanza Kongo's cathedral to a bishopric in 1596, the renamed capital São Salvador developed a dense network of Catholic lay brotherhoods: the Holy Spirit, Our Lady of the Rosary, and Saint Anthony among them. The confraternities organized processions, funded the cathedral's upkeep, ransomed enslaved members, and ran charity for the urban poor. Mwisikongo nobles competed for officerships, making the brotherhoods a parallel civic institution where membership status mattered as much as lineage rank.

conditions.text: Catholicism religion
